aboutPage.title: Creative Youth for Change
aboutPage.subtitle: A forward-thinking youth-led organization aimed toward empowering young individuals around the world. We nurture young people and enable them to work toward a prosperous and just future for everyone.
aboutPage.missionHeading: Education is not a privilege, it is a fundamental right.
aboutPage.missionParagraph1: Our mission is to empower tomorrow's leaders and equip them with the necessary skills and qualities to contribute towards brighter futures. We aim to rear the next generation of change-makers and leaders.
aboutPage.missionParagraph2: Our primary mission is to create an inclusive, welcoming, and supporting environment where young individuals from diverse backgrounds can come together, share different perspectives, celebrate diversity, and work towards common goals. Additionally, our mission aligns with the United Nation Sustainable Development Goals.
aboutPage.visionHeading: Empowering youth today to build a better world tomorrow.
aboutPage.visionParagraph1: We strive to be the leading youth-led organization and amplify youths to be the agents of change in their communities. We believe in the potential of young people and we are certain that they can bring revolutions and positive changes.
aboutPage.visionParagraph2: We are driven by a vision of a world where all young persons have the opportunity to thrive and contribute meaningfully towards the global society.
aboutPage.sdgParagraph1: The United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) are a collection of 17 interlinked global goals designed to be a "greenprint to achieve a better and more sustainable future for all." At Creative Youth for Change, we align our mission and programs with these goals to create meaningful impact.
aboutPage.sdgParagraph2: Our work centers on five SDGs: Quality Education (SDG 4), Gender Equality (SDG 5), Reduced Inequalities (SDG 10), Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions (SDG 16), and Partnerships for the Goals (SDG 17). Together with our additional areas of work, they guide us toward a more equitable and sustainable world.
aboutPage.sdg4Before: We work to ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and to promote lifelong learning opportunities for all. Through our
aboutPage.sdg4After: , we provide free online classes and language learning opportunities for students worldwide, preparing youth for the challenges of tomorrow.
aboutPage.sdg5Before: We strive to achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls. Through our
aboutPage.sdg5After: we empower women and girls to become leaders in their communities, and we advocate for equal rights and opportunities for all genders, especially in marginalized communities.
aboutPage.sdg10Description: We aim to reduce inequality within and among countries. We focus on underrepresented and marginalized communities, ensuring equal access to opportunities.
aboutPage.sdg16Before: We promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development. Our
aboutPage.sdg16After: addresses global challenges and promotes peacebuilding through dialogue, fostering understanding to build peaceful, just societies worldwide. We also work to protect and promote fundamental human rights and dignity for all people.
aboutPage.sdg17Description: We strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development. We collaborate with local and global organizations to amplify our impact and reach more communities, while developing leadership skills and empowering young people to become agents of change in their communities.
aboutPage.childProtectionDescription: We ensure safe environments and opportunities for children to learn and grow. Every child has the right to be protected from harm, abuse, exploitation, and neglect, and to grow up with dignity, respect, and the freedom to reach their full potential.
aboutPage.joinDescription: Support will enable the project to strengthen its existing activities, introduce new educational programs, reach additional learners, and improve the resources available to participants.

educationAsARight.title: Education as a Right
educationAsARight.heading: Education is not a privilege. It's a fundamental right.
educationAsARight.description: Our flagship program providing quality education for students worldwide, with special focus on marginalized girls and women in Afghanistan
educationAsARight.description2: Our main goal is to make education accessible to everyone, mainly to marginalized girls and women in Afghanistan who have been deprived of learning.
educationAsARight.aboutParagraph1: The Education as a Right Project (EaaRP) is a youth-led educational initiative established in August, 2022 to expand access to learning opportunities for students who face barriers to education, particularly young people from marginalized communities in developing countries. A central focus of EaaRP is supporting Afghan girls who have been excluded from formal schooling and academic life, while also providing educational opportunities to marginalized learners across different countries.
educationAsARight.aboutParagraph2: The project has established programs including a University Mentorship Program and a Language Academy, which has offered courses in English, Urdu, Chinese, French, Turkish, and Arabic. Building on this experience, EaaRP now seeks to expand its educational offerings to include STEM courses, leadership and self-development programs, art and design, additional language classes, and preparation for internationally recognized examinations such as TOEFL, IELTS, DET, and SAT. To make this expansion possible and increase the project's reach and effectiveness, EaaRP is seeking funding and other forms of support from suitable partners and funding organizations.
educationAsARight.visionParagraph1: Education provides a foundation for individual development, social participation, economic opportunity, and long-term community development. Yet access to meaningful educational opportunities remains unequal, particularly for young people living in marginalized or challenging circumstances.
educationAsARight.visionParagraph2: Barriers may include limited access to educational institutions, financial constraints, displacement, social restrictions, language barriers, inadequate academic guidance, and limited access to specialized learning opportunities.
educationAsARight.visionParagraph3: For Afghan girls who have been excluded from formal education and academic life, these challenges are particularly significant. When conventional educational pathways become inaccessible, alternative opportunities for continued learning and development become essential.
educationAsARight.visionParagraph4: EaaRP was established to respond to these challenges by creating accessible educational opportunities, academic mentorship, and learning pathways for young people who may otherwise have limited access to them.
educationAsARight.missionParagraph1: The project aims to expand access to inclusive and meaningful educational opportunities for marginalized young people, enabling them to continue learning, develop relevant skills, pursue higher education, and strengthen their capacity to participate in their communities and future opportunities.
educationAsARight.missionIntro: This mission is carried out through some objectives:
educationAsARight.topicAccessDescription: Education as a Right works to expand access to educational opportunities for marginalized students and learners facing barriers to conventional education. The project provides academic mentorship and guidance for students pursuing higher education, while placing particular attention on Afghan girls who have been excluded from formal academic life.
educationAsARight.topicLeadershipDescription: The project creates opportunities for young people to develop the skills, confidence, and knowledge needed to engage actively in their communities and pursue their goals. Through upcoming STEM, leadership, self-development, and art and design programs, it will strengthen interpersonal, creative, and practical skills alongside academic development.
educationAsARight.topicLanguageDescription: EaaRP supports language learning as an essential part of educational access and personal development. By improving opportunities for language education, the project helps learners strengthen their academic communication skills and have access to more educational and professional opportunities.
educationAsARight.universityMentorshipDescription: The University Mentorship Program provides students with guidance and support related to higher education and academic pathways. The program helps learners better understand their educational options and make informed decisions regarding their academic futures.
educationAsARight.languageAcademyDescription: The Language Academy provides language-learning opportunities designed to strengthen communication skills and broaden access to educational and professional opportunities. Languages offered include: English, Urdu, Chinese, French, Turkish and Arabic.
educationAsARight.joinTitle: Join Education as a Right Movement
educationAsARight.joinDescription: Support will enable the project to strengthen its existing activities, introduce new educational programs, reach additional learners, and improve the resources available to participants.

sheLeads.title: She Leads
sheLeads.heading: Empowering women to lead, inspire, and transform.
sheLeads.description: Amplifying the voices of 5,000 Afghan girls and women. Documenting their stories, building their leadership, and advocating for their rights on the global stage.
sheLeads.description2: She Leads exists to unlock the leadership potential of Afghan women and girls. By transforming individual experiences into collective advocacy, the project contributes to a future where women are empowered to lead, create, and make decisions—strengthening families, communities, and society as a whole.
sheLeads.aboutUsParagraph1: She Leads is a youth-initiated project under Creative Youth for Change (CYC). It was developed in response to the increasing restrictions faced by girls and women in Afghanistan. In recent years, Afghan girls have been denied access to education, excluded from public life, and prevented from participating in decisions that affect their futures. She Leads was created to address this reality by offering a safe and credible platform where these voices can be heard, documented, and taken seriously.
sheLeads.aboutUsParagraph2: The project is headed by Miss Tayyaba Sajjad and supported by CYC Founder Mr. Abdul Khaliq Towhidi. What began as concern over the silencing of Afghan women evolved into a structured initiative focused on advocacy, documentation, and leadership development. She Leads is grounded in the belief that meaningful change cannot occur without the direct involvement of those most affected by injustice.
sheLeads.aboutUsParagraph3: At its core, She Leads provides Afghan girls and women with the opportunity to share their lived experiences, including the challenges they face in accessing education, personal freedom, and basic rights. Alongside Afghan participants, the project also engages international allies to strengthen dialogue and advocacy around peace, democracy, and gender equity.
sheLeads.aboutUsParagraph4: One of the project's key objectives is to amplify the voices of 5,000 girls and women and compile their testimonies into a consolidated report to be shared with major international institutions and media platforms, including the United Nations. Through storytelling and strategic outreach, She Leads seeks to maintain sustained global attention on the rights of Afghan women.
sheLeads.visionParagraph1: She Leads envisions a future in which Afghan girls are not exceptions to progress, but leaders within their communities and society. We believe in a future where girls grow up knowing their voices matter, their decisions are respected, and their ambitions are supported rather than restricted.
sheLeads.visionParagraph2: Our vision is rooted in the understanding that Afghan women already possess resilience, intelligence, and leadership capacity. What remains lacking is access to education, opportunity, and platforms where this potential can be recognized and developed.
sheLeads.visionParagraph3: She Leads rejects narratives that portray Afghan women as passive or powerless. Instead, we recognize them as thinkers, innovators, organizers, and decision-makers whose contributions have been constrained by circumstance, not ability.
sheLeads.missionParagraph1: The mission of She Leads is to support and develop the next generation of women leaders in Afghanistan. At a time when girls are being pushed out of schools and public spaces, the project works to ensure that their ambitions continue to grow.
sheLeads.missionIntro: This mission is carried out through three focus areas:
sheLeads.topicTrainingDescription: She Leads emphasizes skill-building and mentorship that takes into account the social and cultural realities Afghan girls face. Through structured learning and guidance, the project creates realistic pathways toward leadership.
sheLeads.topicVoiceDescription: She Leads provides a platform for girls to share their experiences, raise concerns, and propose solutions related to education, rights, and civic participation. Special attention is given to ensuring that marginalized groups, including girls with disabilities, are represented.
sheLeads.topicAdvocacyDescription: By connecting personal experiences with broader advocacy efforts, She Leads works to influence public discourse and policy discussions related to women's rights and leadership in Afghanistan.
sheLeads.joinDescription: Be part of empowering women and girls around the world. Whether you choose to contribute or volunteer your time, your contribution makes a difference in creating a more equitable world.

humanityMatters.title: Humanity Matters
humanityMatters.heading: Understanding is where change begins.
humanityMatters.description: A 2-week online debate program focusing on human rights, peacebuilding, equality, freedom, and democracy with a specific focus on Afghanistan, Palestine, and Ukraine crises.
humanityMatters.aboutParagraph1: Humanity Matters is a two-week online debate and summit program established by Creative Youth for Change, the parent organization of the Education as a Right Project (EaaRP), to bring together human rights advocates, gender equality activists, peacebuilders, ambassadors, and youth change-makers under the theme "Humanity, Peacebuilding, Equality, Freedom, and Democracy."
humanityMatters.aboutParagraph2: Set to launch as an annual program starting in 2027, Humanity Matters will convene student participants and young change-makers alongside UN officials, ambassadors, and established advocates to engage directly with the world's most pressing human rights challenges, with a particular focus on the crises in Afghanistan, Palestine, and Ukraine.
humanityMatters.aboutParagraph3: To make this vision possible and expand its reach and impact, Humanity Matters is seeking funding and partnerships with suitable organizations and supporters.
humanityMatters.visionParagraph1: Real, lasting change begins with honest dialogue and mutual understanding. Yet across the globe, communities facing conflict, displacement, and inequality often find their voices absent from the platforms where decisions about their futures are made.
humanityMatters.visionParagraph2: Barriers to meaningful global dialogue may include restricted access to international platforms, limited representation for affected communities, few opportunities for young advocates to engage directly with policymakers, and a shortage of spaces where activists, officials, and everyday people can speak candidly about complex crises.
humanityMatters.visionParagraph3: Humanity Matters was established to respond to these challenges by creating a platform for open discussion, mutual understanding, and collaborative advocacy among human rights defenders, peacebuilders, and global leaders. We believe that discussion and understanding are essential first steps toward making real, lasting change.
humanityMatters.missionIntro: The project consists of three stages:
humanityMatters.week1Description: Introduction to human rights frameworks, peacebuilding principles, and global challenges
humanityMatters.week2Description: Focused discussions on specific crises and collaborative solution development
humanityMatters.week3Description: Implementation of solutions and continued advocacy through various channels
humanityMatters.joinDescription: Join our global community of change-makers working towards peace, justice, and equality. Your voice and actions can make a real difference.
